output.title: TELNET Protocol Specification
output.abstract: This RFC defines the TELNET protocol which is a standard method for communicating with remote hosts via a network. It specifies the Network Virtual Terminal (NVT) as an abstract character-at-a-time model, the TELNET command set, and connection establishment procedures.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: TELNET is a network protocol used for remote terminal connections. It provides standardized methods to communicate with a remote host over a network.

sections.title: Network Virtual Terminal (NVT)
sections.content: The NVT abstracts common characteristics of various terminal types to provide a consistent interface for remote terminal access.

sections.title: Character Set
sections.content: TELNET uses the USASCII character set by default. The NVT keyboard can generate all 128 USASCII codes and additional keys for specific functions.

key_descriptions.name: CR
key_descriptions.description: Carriage Return - Moves the printer to the beginning of the current line.

key_descriptions.name: LF
key_descriptions.description: Line Feed - Moves the printer to the next line.

key_descriptions.name: FF
key_descriptions.description: Form Feed - Moves the printer to the top of the next page.

key_descriptions.name: Synch
key_descriptions.description: Allows the user to clear their data path to the other party.

key_descriptions.name: Break (BRK)
key_descriptions.description: A signal outside the USASCII set, currently given local meaning within many systems, indicating the Break Key or Attention Key was hit.

key_descriptions.name: Interrupt Process (IP)
key_descriptions.description: Suspends, interrupts, aborts, or terminates the process connected to the NVT.

key_descriptions.name: Abort Output (AO)
key_descriptions.description: Allows the current process to complete without sending output to the user and sends a Synch to the user.

key_descriptions.name: Are You There (AYT)
key_descriptions.description: Requests evidence that the AYT was received, typically in the form of visible characters.

key_descriptions.name: Erase Character (EC)
key_descriptions.description: Deletes the last preceding undeleted character from the data stream.

key_descriptions.name: Erase Line (EL)
key_descriptions.description: Deletes characters from the data stream back to but not including the previous 'CR LF' sequence.

sections.title: TELNET Command Structure
sections.content: All TELNET commands are at least two bytes long: the Interpret as Command (IAC) escape character followed by a command code. Option negotiation commands are three-byte sequences, with the third byte indicating the referenced option.

sections.title: TELNET Commands
sections.content: A list of defined TELNET commands including their codes and meanings.

commands.name: Data Mark
commands.meaning: Part of the Synch, should always be accompanied by a TCP Urgent notification.

commands.name: SB
commands.meaning: Indicates that what follows is subnegotiation of the indicated option.

commands.name: WILL (option code)
commands.meaning: Indicates the desire to begin performing, or confirmation that you are now performing, the indicated option.

commands.name: WON'T (option code)
commands.meaning: Indicates the refusal to perform, or continue performing, the indicated option.

commands.name: DO (option code)
commands.meaning: Indicates the request that the other party perform, or confirmation that you are expecting the other party to perform, the indicated option.

commands.name: DON'T (option code)
commands.meaning: Indicates the demand that the other party stop performing, or confirmation that you are no longer expecting the other party to perform, the indicated option.

sections.title: Connection Establishment
sections.content: The TELNET connection is established between a user's port (U) and the server's well-known port (L=23 for remote terminal access). The server listens on its port L for incoming connections.

port_assignment.comment: Used for remote user access to service hosts (remote terminal access).
